title: Bead-label hook: resolve real branch shapes, and stop dirtying the tree
description:
The bead-labeling hook resolves no bead from an outrigger branch, so a full build-and-ship session on 2026-08-22 in ~/Dev/fathom labeled nothing across three skills.

Two defects, landed together because either alone is worse than both.

1. resolve_bead's candidate regex is [a-z][a-z0-9]*(-[a-z0-9]+)+(\.[0-9]+)*. The + on the hyphen group makes at least one hyphen mandatory, and the leading [a-z] rejects a digit. Reproduced 2026-08-22: branch outrigger/zkc.5/rank-beads-and-reminders-deterministical yields exactly one candidate, the slug, and bd show rejects it. Every short bead id in fathom is hyphen-free, so the hook is blind to every outrigger branch there.

2. refresh_export runs bd export after every successful label, which leaves the tracked tree modified. outrigger's pre-flight and /tadw:ship Step 4 both refuse a dirty tree, and both hit it in that same session while the hook was labeling nothing. Fixing (1) alone converts an intermittent collision into one that fires on every review pass.

Plan: docs/plans/bead-label-hook-resolution-and-visibility.md, M1 and M2. Cite by function name, never by line number (plan section 0).
design:
M1: resolve_bead builds candidates from three ordered sources. Positional first (segment two of a branch with three or more slash-separated segments, which is outrigger's outrigger/<short-id>/<slug>), then the widened pattern [a-z0-9][a-z0-9]*(-[a-z0-9]+)*(\.[0-9]+)*, then a cap of 12 unique candidates longest-first. Verified: the widened pattern emits outrigger, zkc.5, and the slug against the real branch.

M2: refresh_export skips the export unless the export file is already modified, or TADW_BEAD_LABEL_EXPORT=1 is set. bv reads the database directly, so it costs bv nothing; the env var covers Manifest, whose reader is unconfirmed.

M2 inverts a committed test that asserts the opposite, so the test change ships in the same commit or the pre-push hook blocks the push.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Branch outrigger/zkc.5/rank-beads-and-reminders-deterministical resolves to the bead whose short id is zkc.5. This is the regression case for the whole outage.
2. Branch feature/tadw-alpha-one/x still resolves, so the widened pattern breaks nothing the seven existing add_branch cases cover.
3. Branch main resolves nothing, returns non-zero, and logs.
4. A branch whose slug alone matches a real bead resolves the positional segment first, not the slug.
5. A branch offering more than twelve candidate tokens issues at most twelve bd show probes, asserted against recorded argv.
6. On a clean tree, a labeled skill runs bd update and no bd export. This replaces label/bd: refreshes the export instead of committing it, which asserts the opposite.
7. With TADW_BEAD_LABEL_EXPORT=1, the export runs.
8. With .beads/issues.jsonl already modified, the export runs without the env var.
9. After case 6, git status --porcelain is empty.
10. bash hooks/test-claude-scripts.sh passes with zero failures.
close_reason: Implemented on branch outrigger/tadw-b14/hook-resolution-and-visibility; 173 checks pass and each fix was observed to fail against the pre-fix script

title: Sanitize git env vars in the pre-push hook before running checks
description:
## Why (Computational)

git runs the pre-push hook with GIT_DIR exported. From the main checkout the value is the relative path .git, so a fixture-building test that runs git -C <tmpdir> init resolves it under the tmpdir and stays isolated. From a linked worktree (.claude/worktrees/...) the value is an absolute path, -C does not redirect it, and the fixture's git init re-initializes the MAIN repository's gitdir as bare. Observed on 2026-08-14: a push from a linked worktree left the main .git/config with core.bare=true and core.excludesFile=/dev/null (the latter written by test_changed_set.py's fixture at skills/quality-gates/scripts/test_changed_set.py:116), which broke every work-tree git operation in both checkouts until repaired by hand. The corrupting suites are test_changed_set.py, test_check_secrets.py, and test_check_hygiene.py, all of which build git fixtures and all of which the pre-push hook runs.

The stakeholder is anyone who pushes from a Claude Code worktree, which is how agent sessions push.

## Fix sketch

Unset GIT_DIR, GIT_WORK_TREE, GIT_INDEX_FILE, GIT_COMMON_DIR, GIT_OBJECT_DIRECTORY, and GIT_PREFIX at the top of .githooks/pre-push before any check runs (the hook's cwd is the worktree root, so git re-discovers correctly). Belt and suspenders: the fixture helpers in the three test scripts can also pass env={...} scrubbed of GIT_* to subprocess.run, so running a suite directly under any GIT_DIR is safe too.

## Estimated size

2-4 files, about 20 LOC, band: Target.
close_reason: Fixed in 1e5517a: the pre-push hook unsets the six GIT_* variables before its first git call, the three fixture suites clear the same names at import, and test_prepush.py gained a linked-worktree case that fails without the hook change

title: Give the .claude/scripts hooks a test harness
description:
## Why (Computational)

The three hooks in `.claude/scripts/` have no automated coverage, and they are the most dangerous
code in this repository: `autocommit_beads_after_br.sh` (since deleted) and `label_bead_on_skill_invocation.sh`
both ran `git commit` and `git push` to main, and `close_bead_on_pr_merge.sh` closes a bead and
pushes. `hooks/test-hooks.js` covers the style-core hooks only, so nothing here tests these.

That gap is not theoretical. A fresh-eyes pass over commit 9ce0f8a found six defects across the
three scripts, and f8259ea fixed all six with manual verification and no pinned tests. Two of the
six were guards that read as active and never fired, which is exactly the class a test catches and
a reading does not:

- `close_bead_on_pr_merge.sh` matched bead ids with `[a-z]+-[a-z0-9]{2,8}`, which extracts
  `tadw-qg` from `tadw-qg-script-secrets-gate-jbg`. The hook could never close a bead here, and it
  had shipped that way.
- Its `status == "unknown"` guard never fired, because `bd show <missing-id> --json` writes to
  stderr and leaves stdout empty, so `|| echo unknown` produced the empty string instead.

The stakeholder is anyone who trusts these hooks to move tracker state. A silently inert hook
means beads stay open and someone closes them by hand without knowing why.

## Estimated size

2 files, about 300 LOC, band: Stretch.

Stretch is justified because a harness with no cases is not a harness. The fake `bd`, `git`, and
`gh` on PATH are the load-bearing part, and they only prove themselves against real cases.
design:
One `hooks/test-claude-scripts.sh` (or a Node peer of `hooks/test-hooks.js`, if that
reads better beside the existing suite), plus a registration line in the AGENTS.md command block.

The load-bearing design decision is how to run a hook that shells out to `bd`, `git`, `gh`, and
`jq` without touching the real tracker or the real remote. Three rules:

1. FAKE THE TOOLS ON PATH, do not mock inside the scripts. Each case builds a temp dir holding
   executable `bd`, `git`, and `gh` stubs, then prepends it to PATH. The scripts stay unmodified,
   so the test exercises the shipped code rather than a test-only branch. A stub records the
   argv it received to a file, which is how a case asserts what the hook tried to do.
2. NEVER let a case reach the network or the real repo. `git push` in a stub is a no-op that
   records. A case that would push asserts against the recording, not against a remote.
3. FEED REAL PAYLOAD SHAPES on stdin. The hooks read a Claude Code hook payload, so a case
   passes the same JSON shape the runtime sends: `hook_event_name`, `tool_input.command`,
   `tool_input.skill`, `tool_response.stderr`.

Assert on three observable things, in this order of value: the exit status (always 0, since every
failure path is designed to let the session continue), the recorded argv of `bd` and `git`, and
the stderr log lines.

Pin the six f8259ea fixes specifically. Each case should fail when its fix is reverted, and the
bead is not done until that has been checked per case rather than assumed.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Given the harness, when it runs with no `bd`, `git`, or `gh` on the real PATH beyond its own stubs, then every case passes and no case reaches a network or the real .beads database.
2. Given a payload whose command is `bd update x --claim && bd show x`, when the autocommit hook runs, then the recorded argv shows it reached the commit path, and reverting the subcommand-detection fix makes that case fail.
3. Given a payload whose command is `bd show x`, when the autocommit hook runs, then no `git commit` is recorded.
4. Given a merged PR whose title names `tadw-qg-script-secrets-gate-jbg`, when the close hook runs, then the recorded argv closes that full id, and reverting the id-regex fix makes the case fail.
5. Given a merged PR whose body names two real beads and carries no `Bead:` trailer, when the close hook runs, then no `bd update --status=closed` is recorded and the log says it refused.
6. Given a merged PR whose body carries a `Bead: <id>` trailer that disagrees with the title, when the close hook runs, then the trailer id is the one closed.
7. Given a `bd show` stub that prints its error to stderr and nothing to stdout, when the close hook runs, then no close is recorded, and reverting the empty-status guard makes the case fail.
8. Given a worktree checkout on main, when either the close hook or the label hook runs, then the recorded argv reaches the canonical tracker. (Retired 2026-08-21: `bd` takes no `--db` pin, so the worktree cases now assert that no call carries one.)
9. Given a gate-mode marker named `<label>__<id>` for a label other than `qa-d`, when the Stop handler runs against a passing report, then that label is applied and not `qa-d`.
10. Given every case, when the suite finishes, then it prints a real pass and fail count and exits non-zero on any failure.
11. Given AGENTS.md, when reading "Commands for This Repo", then the harness appears there and its path resolves on disk.
notes:
## Done when (Acceptance)

- A single command runs the whole harness, and it is listed in the AGENTS.md command block
- The three hooks are unmodified by this bead: the harness fakes tools on PATH rather than adding
  a test-only branch to shipped code
- No case touches the real `.beads` database, the real git remote, or the network
- Each of the six f8259ea fixes has a case that was OBSERVED to fail with the fix reverted, not
  assumed to. Record the observation in the commit message the way f8259ea recorded its manual runs
- The suite reports real counts and exits non-zero on failure

## Out of scope

- The `gate` mode QA-report path beyond criterion 9. Gate mode is dormant in this repository,
  because it reads `.gstack/qa-reports/` and `/qa` is a gstack skill. Criterion 9 covers the label
  plumbing, which is the part f8259ea changed. Full report-parsing coverage is a separate bead if
  gstack is ever installed here.
- A pre-push hook that runs this harness. That belongs to tadw-qg-prepush-hook-suites-w8r, which
  already owns the AGENTS.md command list as its input.

## Provenance

Filed after `/verify-acceptance` graded commit f8259ea INCONCLUSIVE for the hook half, on the
ground that no bead recorded what those three scripts had to achieve. The criteria above were
written from the defects found, so treat them as regression coverage rather than as a
specification the fixes were built against.

## Amended 2026-08-21 (tracker cutover)

The tool name above is now `bd`; the earlier CLI is gone from this repository. Two criteria lost
their subject with it and are retired rather than met:

- Criteria 2 and 3 tested `autocommit_beads_after_br.sh`, which was deleted. It existed only
  because that tracker wrote its state into a git-tracked export; `bd` writes to a gitignored
  database, so there is nothing to auto-commit.
- Criterion 8 tested the `--db` pin, which `bd` does not take. The worktree cases that replaced it
  assert the same guarantee from the other side: a hook run from a worktree still reaches the
  canonical tracker, and no call carries a `--db`.

The suite is now 60 checks, down from 63.
close_reason: hooks/test-claude-scripts.sh: 63 checks over 22 cases, registered in AGENTS.md and .githooks/pre-push. All 8 fixes observed to fail against a reverted copy. Deviation recorded: git is real behind a recording stub rather than fully faked, because a git reimplementation would be the wrong subject under test.

title: Add a pre-push hook that runs the repository's checks
description:
## Why (Computational)

`AGENTS.md` lists nine commands under "Commands for This Repo", and running them is a
convention, not a mechanism. The only hard gate in this repository is
`.githooks/reference-transaction`, which fires on `v*` tags alone, so commits and pushes ride
entirely on the session remembering.

The stakeholder is the author who pushes a broken formatter or a failing suite and finds out
late, or never.

Author direction, recorded as D4 in the plan: enforcement is a local git hook, not GitHub
Actions. `.github/workflows/lint.yml` keeps the checks it runs today and gains nothing new.

Plan: docs/plans/quality-gates-hardening.md (M2)

## Estimated size

2 files, about 130 LOC, band: Target.
design:
One POSIX sh `.githooks/pre-push`, modeled on the existing
`reference-transaction` hook, running the `AGENTS.md` command list minus `evals/run.py`.

Three deliberate behaviors carry the design:

1. Run every check even after one fails, then report all failures together. A hook that stops at
   the first failure makes the author push, fail, fix, push, fail again.
2. A missing tool warns and allows, naming the tool. This follows the precedent
   `reference-transaction` set for a missing `claude`: an unpushable clone is worse than an
   unchecked push, and `rumdl` and `node` are not universally installed.
3. `TADW_PREPUSH=off` is a documented escape rather than an undocumented workaround, documented
   the way `TADW_STYLE_CORE=off` already is.

`evals/run.py` is excluded because each case is a real model call, far too slow and too expensive
to sit on a push.

A push that only deletes refs has nothing to check, so allow it. Keep output quiet on success:
one summary line, not ten.

`AGENTS.md` has a "Release gate (one-time setup per clone)" section documenting
`git config core.hooksPath .githooks`. Broaden it to cover both hooks rather than adding a second
setup section, since one `core.hooksPath` call now serves both.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Given a throwaway clone with `core.hooksPath` set and a badly formatted markdown file, when `git push --dry-run` runs, then the push is refused and the output names that file.
2. Given `TADW_PREPUSH=off` in the environment, when the same push runs, then it proceeds.
3. Given `rumdl` absent from PATH, when the push runs, then it proceeds and the output names `rumdl` as skipped.
4. Given two failing checks, when the push runs, then both failures appear in the output.
5. Given the diff against the base, when inspecting `.github/workflows/lint.yml`, then it is unchanged.
6. Given a push that only deletes a remote ref, when the hook runs, then it allows the push without running the suites.
notes:
## Done when (Acceptance)

- `.githooks/pre-push` exists, is executable, and is POSIX sh
- Breaking one file's formatting makes a push fail and names that file
- `TADW_PREPUSH=off` lets the same push through
- A missing tool warns by name and allows
- Two simultaneous failures both appear; the hook does not stop at the first
- `AGENTS.md` documents both hooks under one setup section
- `.github/workflows/lint.yml` is unchanged
- The hook's wall time is measured and stated in the `AGENTS.md` section

## Out of scope

The verdict-gating stage. That is the "Gate the push on a recorded FAIL verdict" bead, which
appends a second stage to this same file.
close_reason: done

title: Gate the push on a recorded FAIL verdict
description:
## Why (Computational)

A session can run the gates, get a FAIL, and push anyway, leaving no trace and
hitting no barrier. "Landing the Plane" in `AGENTS.md` tells the session to run the gates before
pushing, but nothing checks that it did, or what it found.

The stakeholder is the author's future self, and anyone who pulls a commit that its own QA said
was not fit to ship.

Plan: docs/plans/quality-gates-hardening.md (M4)

## Estimated size

2 files, about 70 LOC, band: Target.
design:
Append a second stage to the `.githooks/pre-push` file the suite-running bead
created. Git calls exactly one `pre-push` hook, so two responsibilities on the same event must
share a file with separate stages.

Read `quality-gates-report.json` from `$(git rev-parse --git-dir)` through `python3 -c`; do not
parse JSON in sh, and do not hardcode `.git/`. The writing skill resolves the same way, and the
reason is worktrees: `--git-dir` returns a distinct path per linked worktree, so each worktree's
hook reads that worktree's own verdict. A literal `.git/` is a file rather than a directory inside
a worktree, and `--git-common-dir` would let every worktree overwrite the others' verdict.
Verified 2026-08-11 with a three-worktree probe: a pre-push hook run from each worktree resolved
its own git dir and read its own planted report.

The forgiveness rules are the design, not an afterthought:

- No report, or an unreadable report, warns and allows. Absence is not evidence of a problem, and
  blocking there would make the hook unusable for documentation pushes and teach people to
  disable it.
- Only a recorded verdict of FAIL blocks. The message names the verdict, the recorded head, and
  the timestamp, plus both exits: re-run `/quality-gates`, or set `TADW_PREPUSH=off`.
- A verdict whose recorded head is not an ancestor of the pushed commit warns as stale, using
  `git merge-base --is-ancestor`, but still allows.

Then add one line to `AGENTS.md` "Landing the Plane" step 4 noting the refusal.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Given a `.git/quality-gates-report.json` with verdict FAIL, when `git push --dry-run` runs in a throwaway clone, then the push is refused and the output names the verdict, the head, and the timestamp.
2. Given no report file, when the push runs, then it proceeds and prints exactly one warning line.
3. Given a report whose recorded head is not an ancestor of the pushed commit, when the push runs, then it proceeds and prints a staleness warning.
4. Given a report with verdict PASS whose head is current, when the push runs, then it proceeds silently.
5. Given the repository, when `node hooks/test-hooks.js` runs, then it passes.
notes:
## Done when (Acceptance)

- A hand-written FAIL report refuses a dry-run push in a throwaway clone
- `TADW_PREPUSH=off` lets that push through
- No report file means one warning line and a successful push
- Both stages live in one `.githooks/pre-push` and report separately
- `AGENTS.md` "Landing the Plane" step 4 notes the refusal
- `node hooks/test-hooks.js` still passes
close_reason: Stage 2 of .githooks/pre-push reads the recorded verdict and refuses a FAIL. 30 checks in test_prepush.py, all criteria graded ACCEPTED.

title: Fix the command/skill namespace collision in all 18 commands that delegate with 'load the skill'
description:
A command file and a skill directory that share a name also share one `tadw:` invocation namespace, and the command wins. When such a command's body says "Use the `<name>` skill", invoking it returns the command body, whose first line redirects to itself, so the skill is never loaded.

This is not theoretical. `/bead-audit-all` shipped this way and every backlog sweep it ran scored from a twenty-line summary instead of the 661-line rubric, reporting confident numbers computed from nothing. A wrong number produced this way is indistinguishable downstream from a right one, which is what makes the class dangerous rather than merely untidy.

18 commands collide by name, and the triage below shows all 18 delegate. `/bead-audit-all` is not one of them: no `skills/bead-audit-all/` exists, so it never collided. Its 2.4.1 fix is the pattern to copy, not a reduction of the work.

## Triage result (completed 2026-08-09)

All 18 colliding commands delegate by name. **Zero are self-contained.** An earlier read of this bead assumed body length was a proxy for safety; it is not. Commands with 10 to 20 lines of their own instructions still open with "Use the `<name>` skill", so they redirect exactly like the one-line ones.

Total skill content unreachable by name: **271,067 bytes.**

| Command | Skill bytes shadowed |
|---|---|
| /bead-audit | 51,113 |
| /plan-to-beads | 31,438 |
| /ux-audit-ios | 22,598 |
| /product-surface-docs | 18,979 |
| /ux-audit | 18,291 |
| /plan-review | 16,858 |
| /ab-test-design | 13,614 |
| /product-roadmap | 12,830 |
| /product-research | 12,492 |
| /research-ingest | 12,193 |
| /agentic-clean-code | 11,288 |
| /competitive-analysis | 10,702 |
| /product-brief | 9,257 |
| /aso-audit | 8,933 |
| /verify-acceptance | 8,314 |
| /roadmap-dashboard | 7,596 |
| /business-ideas | 2,740 |
| /idea-wizard | 1,831 |

Classification test used: the command body matches `(use|load|invoke) the \`?<name>\`? skill` and contains no `SKILL.md` read. Reproduce it by re-running that match over `commands/` against the `skills/` directory names.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run `/bead-audit` on any bead, in a session with the plugin loaded.
2. Watch which file the Skill tool returns. It is `commands/bead-audit.md` (20 lines), not `skills/bead-audit/SKILL.md` (661 lines).
3. Confirm the substitution directly: the returned body carries the resolved `$ARGUMENTS` value, which only a command receives.

Expected: the audit rubric loads. Actual: the command body loads and redirects to itself.

The 18 colliding names, from `comm -12` over `commands/` and `skills/`: ab-test-design, agentic-clean-code, aso-audit, bead-audit, business-ideas, competitive-analysis, idea-wizard, plan-review, plan-to-beads, product-brief, product-research, product-roadmap, product-surface-docs, research-ingest, roadmap-dashboard, ux-audit, ux-audit-ios, verify-acceptance.

## Why the runtime does this

`claude plugin details tadw` reports 72 registered skills for 35 skill directories and 37 commands. Commands and skills occupy one namespace, and each colliding name holds two entries. The cost table shows both, for example `plan-review ~50 always-on ~6.2k on-invoke` (the skill) beside `plan-review ~50 always-on ~330 on-invoke` (the command). The command's description is the one surfaced to the model.
design:
Three fixes exist, and the choice is per command. The triage is done, so every one of the 18 needs one of them.

**A. Read the skill from disk.** Replace the delegating line with an explicit `Read` of `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`, plus a `Glob` fallback and an assertion that named headings are present in the file that was read. This is what `/response-style` and `/bead-audit-all` do. Keeps the command name. Costs a hardcoded path per command, forever, and the pattern must be remembered for every command written afterward.

**C. Delete the command and let the skill take the name.** Verified empirically on 2026-08-09: `commands/competitive-analysis.md` was moved out of the installed plugin, the registered skill count fell from 72 to 71, the surviving entry kept the skill's on-invoke cost (~3.9k, not the command's ~0.1k), and after a restart the slash menu showed the skill's own description ("Deep competitor teardown with positioning map, moat analysis, feature gaps..."). The file was restored and the plugin re-validated at exit 0.

Nothing is lost that matters. `$ARGUMENTS` still works, since four skills already use it. Only `argument-hint` is lost, which is a menu display hint rather than behavior. Deleting also repairs the agents: `agents/product-manager.md` tells itself to load these same skills by name and hits the identical dead end today.

**B. Rename one side.** Give the command a distinct name so no collision exists. This is what 19 of the 37 commands already do (`/fresh-eyes-cr` for `review-fresh-eyes`, `/prod-ops` for `production-ops`). Breaks any hardcoded invocation path in other repos.

**Recommended: C for any command whose content is skill content, A for any command that carries genuine per-invocation instructions worth keeping under a slash name.** C is preferred by default because it removes the collision rather than working around it, and costs nothing afterward.

The governing rule to encode: **a command may share a skill's name, or delegate to that skill by name, but never both.**

Sequence. Fix `/bead-audit` first, since 2.4.1 ships a README callout telling users to avoid it. For each remaining command, decide C or A by asking whether the body says anything that is not already the skill's job; most of it (for example `/ux-audit` naming the `ux-product-designer` role) reads like skill content and should move into the skill before the command is deleted.

Guard against regression with a check in `hooks/test-hooks.js`, which already asserts that `/response-style` reads its skill file rather than invoking it. Generalize that check to every colliding name.
acceptance_criteria:
1. MET. Every one of the 18 colliding names is resolved: 8 by deletion (7 in 2.5.0 plus /bead-audit in 2.4.2), 10 by reading the SKILL.md from disk. Re-running the triage match over commands/ returns zero.
2. MET. Nothing needed moving. Each deleted command's body was a precis of its skill; /business-ideas and /idea-wizard duplicated a step already at line 12 of their own SKILL.md. The commits name this per command.
3. MET, 2026-08-09, after installing 2.5.0 and restarting. The menu shows the skill's own description for bead-audit ("against the Marr audit, size audit, type-specific section audit, and a grounding audit against the current main branch") rather than the deleted command's ("against the Marr, size, and type-specific section standards"). Verified by resolution rather than by grepping the loaded body; the description comes from the skill's frontmatter, so the file being read is the skill.
4. MET. Check 18 in hooks/test-hooks.js. Proven to discriminate, not merely to pass: injecting a delegate-by-name regression into /ux-audit exits 1 naming that command; removing only its Glob fallback exits 1 naming that; restoring leaves the file byte-identical and the suite green.
5. AMENDED, then MET. Originally: "a registered skill count equal to (skill directories + surviving commands), with no name appearing twice." The count holds: 64 = 35 + 29. The second clause does not, and it was wrong when written. It assumed every collision would be eliminated; the chosen design keeps 10 commands that share a name and read from disk, so those 10 names register twice on purpose. Amended clause: no name may appear twice unless its command reads the skill from disk, which check 18 enforces.
6. MET. The /bead-audit callout in README.md now says the command file was removed and the skill takes the slash name. AGENTS.md carries the namespace rule instead of the "only /bead-audit-all has been fixed" wording.
7. MET. rumdl fmt --check . clean over 106 files; 19 hook checks pass with the docs/HOOKS.md count verified; claude plugin validate . exits 0; 25 framework-leak checks pass.
8. MET. business-ideas and idea-wizard are referenced by no agent and no command. Accepted and recorded in AGENTS.md: both are invoked directly as /<name>, so a referrer would add nothing. No other skill was orphaned; 33 of 35 remain referenced.
notes:
Done when every command that collides with a same-named skill either loads that skill's real content or does not claim to, and a test fails if a new delegating collision is introduced.

Triage is complete as of 2026-08-09: all 18 delegate, none are self-contained, so the size is no longer provisional. The earlier 'Stretch (provisional)' band assumed only a subset would need work.

Not done when the 18 are merely surveyed. The survey is finished; the edits are the deliverable.

Option C (delete the command, let the skill take the name) was verified empirically on 2026-08-09 by moving commands/competitive-analysis.md out of the installed plugin and restarting. Details in the Design field.
close_reason: done

title: Add a publish-plugin skill that cuts and tags a release
description:
Publishing this plugin is entirely manual and it drifts. plugin.json sat at 2.10.1 while main ran 13 commits past the release commit, and the v2.10.0 and v2.10.1 tags were created locally and never pushed. The only automation in the path is a gate: .githooks/reference-transaction refuses a v* tag when 'claude plugin validate' fails. There is no release workflow and no publish script, and 'gh release list' returns nothing.

The marketplace pins tadw at version 'latest' against this repository's git URL, so pushing main is what actually publishes. That makes an untagged, unversioned main a published state, which is why the drift is worth closing with a skill rather than a checklist.
design:
Decide the semver bump from the changes since the last release, not from a person's mood. MAJOR for a renamed or removed component, a changed plugin name (the invocation namespace), or a broken machine-readable contract. MINOR for a new skill, agent, command, flag, or environment variable. PATCH for a fix, a doc edit, or a test-only change.

The version bump lands as its own 'chore(release): X.Y.Z' commit on main touching exactly CHANGELOG.md and .claude-plugin/plugin.json, after any feature branch has been squash-merged. Every prior release in this repository has that shape, and releases here batch several landings, so the bump cannot be tied to one branch's squash. The tag then points at a tree whose manifest states the version it claims.
acceptance_criteria:
1. skills/publish-plugin/SKILL.md exists and 'claude plugin validate .' parses its frontmatter.
2. The skill derives the bump from the commits and diff since the last tag, and states the rule that decided it.
3. The skill writes the CHANGELOG version heading and the compare link footer in the existing Keep a Changelog shape.
4. The skill updates version in .claude-plugin/plugin.json and commits both files as 'chore(release): X.Y.Z'.
5. The skill squash-merges a feature branch when given one, by delegating to the ship skill rather than reimplementing the land.
6. The skill tags vX.Y.Z and pushes main and the tag, and treats the reference-transaction refusal as a stop.
7. The skill is registered in the AGENTS.md name list, the AGENTS.md routing table, the README skills table, and docs/ROUTING.md, and is listed among the accepted orphans.
8. The repository's own check list passes.
close_reason: shipped: feat: Add a publish-plugin skill that cuts and tags a release (tadw-muo)

title: Stub every hook check in the pre-push fixtures
description:
## Why (Computational)

`.githooks/test_prepush.py` is 79.5s of a 148.7s ship gate, the single largest cost in the repository's own checks.

Profiled 2026-08-23: building a fixture costs 0.28s of git work, and one `git push --dry-run` costs 2.41s with the hook and 0.03s with `TADW_PREPUSH=off`. The suite makes 31 real pushes. So the cost is not the fixtures and not git; it is the hook's own checks running inside every push.

The fixture stubs 8 of the 14 checks. The remaining 6 are real, and they sum to roughly 2.3s: two style-testing scripts, two doc-path scripts, the secret scanner, and rumdl.

Re-running this repository's linters 31 times inside a suite proves nothing their own suites do not already prove, and all of those suites run in the same gate anyway.
design:
Derive the stub set from `commands_in_hook()` rather than listing it. Every hook command naming a path in this tree gets a body that exits 0, keyed by its interpreter. A check added to the hook is then stubbed automatically, which is what the current hardcoded SLOW_CHECKS map cannot do.

rumdl stays real: it is a binary rather than a file in the tree, so there is nothing to stub, and it costs 0.1s.

The suite's subject is the hook's control flow, which checks fail, which warn, which are skipped, whether a deletion is gated. Not whether the linters work.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Given the suite, when it runs, then every check the hook invokes by path is stubbed in the fixture.
2. Given a check added to .githooks/pre-push, when the suite runs, then it is stubbed without editing the suite.
3. Given the suite, when it runs, then all 30 checks still pass.
4. Given the suite, when timed, then it completes in under 40 seconds, down from 79.5.
5. Given the repository, when the full check list runs, then every command still exits 0.

title: Bead-label hook wiring errors on every event when $CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR no longer exists
description:
A session whose worktree is removed under it keeps running, and $CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR then names a directory that is gone. Every wired event fails at the shell level: /bin/sh reports 'No such file or directory' and exits 127, so Claude Code surfaces 'Stop hook error', 'UserPromptSubmit hook error', and 'PostToolUse:Bash hook error' on nearly every turn.

Observed 2026-08-23. A live claude process (PID 86028, started 2026-08-22) had cwd /Users/jtempleton/Dev/templeton-agentic-dev-workbench/.outrigger/worktrees/qg-prepush-verdict-gate-tug-gate-the-push-on-a-recorded-fail-verdict, which .outrigger/worktrees/ no longer contains. The scripts are tracked in git, so the copy existed while the worktree did; landing tadw-qg-prepush-verdict-gate-tug removed the worktree while the session lived on.

The hook itself is careful: every failure path inside it exits 0 so a session continues. The wiring is not, because the shell never reaches the script. So the one failure the design took most care to avoid is the one the wiring produces.
design:
Guard each wired command with a test for an executable file, and exit 0 when it is absent. Write the path twice rather than binding it to a shell variable, since a hook command string is not a place to rely on Claude Code leaving $-expansion alone.

Apply it in three places, so a repository installed later inherits the guard:
  1. .claude/settings.json here, for all four entries (three label events plus the PostToolUse close hook).
  2. HOOK_COMMAND in scripts/install_label_bead_on_skill_invocation.sh.
  3. Cases in hooks/test-claude-scripts.sh.

The installer identifies its own wiring with contains($name), so the guarded string is still recognized, repaired rather than duplicated, and reported as wired by --check.

Silence is the right outcome here rather than a warning: the script that owns the log file is the missing thing, so there is nowhere to record the outage from. Restarting the session is the fix, and the guard only stops the noise.
acceptance_criteria:
1. With $CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR pointing at a directory that does not exist, the wired command exits 0 and writes nothing to stdout or stderr.
2. With the script present, the wired command still runs it and still labels the bead.
3. install --check reports all three events wired against the guarded command string.
4. A second installer run still reports 'already wired' and adds no duplicate entry.
5. bash hooks/test-claude-scripts.sh passes with zero failures.
6. AGENTS.md records what a removed project directory does and what stops it.
notes: Not a fix for the zombie session that found it: a session whose project directory is gone cannot label anything, guard or no guard. End that session. The guard is about every future session that outlives its worktree.
close_reason: shipped: fix: guard hook commands against a missing project dir (tadw-1rf)

title: Bead-label hook: close the drift between source and deployed copies
description:
Deployed copies of label_bead_on_skill_invocation.sh drift from the source in scripts/, and nothing reports how. The installer already reports installed / updated / already current by comparing source against destination with cmp, so drift DETECTION exists. What is missing is narrower: it never says WHAT differs, and it has no way to report drift without overwriting it.

Re-checked 2026-08-22 at main 141440f: this repository's own two copies are now byte-identical at 465 lines, so the in-repo drift the plan recorded is already closed. Fathom's copy is 18,293 bytes and carries no br references, so the br removal the plan scheduled is also already done there.

Plan: docs/plans/bead-label-hook-resolution-and-visibility.md, M4. Re-verify both claims before starting, since both were true of an older tree.
design:
1. Add a content hash near the top of the script, computed at install time by the installer and logged on every run. A hash rather than a VERSION string, because a hash self-maintains and a version needs a bump discipline nothing here enforces.

2. Extend the installer rather than rebuild it. Print a one-line summary of what differs before overwriting, and add a --check flag that reports drift and exits non-zero without copying, so a pre-push hook can use it later.

3. Reinstall into fathom, then confirm fathom's own suite still passes.

Do not add a tracker backend. bd only.
acceptance_criteria:
1. The installer run twice reports 'already current' the second time and copies nothing.
2. The installer against a modified destination reports what differs before overwriting.
3. --check exits non-zero against a drifted destination and copies nothing.
4. --check exits 0 against a current destination.
5. diff between the source and each deployed copy is empty, and the logged hash matches.
6. bash hooks/test-claude-scripts.sh passes with zero failures here, and uv run pytest -q passes in fathom.
notes:
Steps 1 and 2 landed in 14ac7f9: the runtime content hash and the installer's --check plus its drift report. Step 3 needed nothing: both copies here were already byte-identical with all three events wired.

Step 4, reinstalling into fathom, is NOT done and needs the author's call. --check reports fathom's copy carries 54 lines the source does not, and those 54 lines are an UNCOMMITTED local edit, so a reinstall would discard work that exists nowhere else. atlas is 116 lines ahead of the source in the same way, and AGENTS.md still calls atlas 'the copy of record', which conflicts with treating scripts/ here as the source. Settle which repository is the source before overwriting either.
close_reason: All four copies converged on hash 15885ca18df1 (source, this repo's deployed copy, fathom, atlas), all three events wired in each. Drift closed in both directions: fathom's prefix filter was ported up rather than overwritten.

title: Bead-label hook: make a broken hook visible
description:
The hook's header states its contract: every failure path logs to stderr and exits 0, so a skill runs whether or not the bead could be labeled. Exiting 0 is right. Logging only to stderr is what makes an outage undetectable, because hook stderr is not surfaced in normal use.

This has hidden a total outage twice. The deployed copy's own comment records the first: every label attempt between the 2026-08-12 cutover and that fix logged a failure nobody read, and no bead was labeled in that window. The second is the outrigger resolution defect (tadw-b14), found by inspection after the fact rather than by anything in the session.

Plan: docs/plans/bead-label-hook-resolution-and-visibility.md, M3. Cite by function name, never by line number.
design:
1. Append every invocation outcome to $GIT_COMMON/bead-label.log: timestamp, event, skill, branch, resolved id or 'unresolved', action taken. Keep stderr logging unchanged. Cap the file by truncating to its last 1000 lines when it exceeds that, checked once per invocation. The hook fires on every /simplify and /code-review in a long-lived checkout, so unbounded growth is unacceptable and a rotation scheme is more machinery than the problem needs.

2. Add a --doctor mode that resolves against the current branch and prints what it would do, writing nothing: no label, no export, no log line. It takes no hook payload on stdin and no arguments; it reads the current branch itself. Guard it before the payload read at the bottom of the script, so a missing stdin cannot hang it.

Preserve the exit-0-on-every-failure contract. This adds visibility, not a failure mode.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Every invocation appends exactly one line to $GIT_COMMON/bead-label.log, carrying the branch, the resolved id or 'unresolved', and the action.
2. An unresolved run still exits 0 and still writes its line.
3. --doctor on a resolvable branch names the bead and the label, calls no bd update, and writes no log line.
4. --doctor on main reports no candidate and exits 0.
5. The log truncates to its last 1000 lines once it exceeds that.
6. bash hooks/test-claude-scripts.sh passes with zero failures.
close_reason: Implemented on branch outrigger/tadw-b14/hook-resolution-and-visibility; 173 checks pass and each fix was observed to fail against the pre-fix script

title: Take the response-style evals out of the ship gate
description:
## Why (Computational)

The `ship` skill takes its gate from the AGENTS.md "Commands for This Repo" block: 'When it declares a list, the list is the gate and every command in it must exit 0.' That block ends with `python3 evals/run.py`, so the response-style evals gate every merge.

They are the wrong shape for a gate on two counts. They are non-deterministic: `plain-sentences` grades model prose against a 35-word ceiling, and observed lengths across runs on 2026-08-22 and 2026-08-23 were 40, 38, 37, 34, 26, and 22. A gate that fails at random teaches people to re-run until green, which is how a gate stops meaning anything. They also cost twelve real model calls and several minutes per run.

Measured this session: two finished, fully verified branches were blocked by that suite, once on a credential fault and once on a grader fault, neither of which the branches caused.

AGENTS.md already excludes three commands from `.githooks/pre-push` and says why for each. The ship gate has no such statement, so it takes the whole list.

The stakeholder is anyone shipping through /tadw:ship.
design:
State the ship gate in AGENTS.md the way the pre-push exclusions are already stated: in prose, beside the list, with the reason. Do not delete the command from the block. It is a real command for this repository and removing it would hide it, and `.githooks/test_prepush.py` asserts every NOT_IN_HOOK key is still present in AGENTS.md, so a deletion would correctly fail that check.

The evals stay a measurement you run deliberately, not a gate that runs on every merge.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Given AGENTS.md, when the ship skill reads it for a gate, then the text names the gate as the list minus python3 evals/run.py, with the reason.
2. Given AGENTS.md, when a reader looks for the evals command, then it is still in the command block.
3. Given the repository, when python3 .githooks/test_prepush.py runs, then it passes, including its assertion that every documented exclusion is still in AGENTS.md.
4. Given the repository, when python3 skills/quality-gates/scripts/check_doc_paths.py runs, then every path claim still resolves.
close_reason: shipped: chore: take the response-style evals out of the ship gate (tadw-gcc)

title: Grade decision-matrix-trigger on the rule, not on bold markup
description:
## Why (Computational)

`evals/cases/decision-matrix-trigger` has been marked `known_failing` since 2026-08-05 and fails on every run, in both arms. Because `python3 evals/run.py` is in the AGENTS.md check list, it is the ship gate for every branch, so one red case blocks every merge in the repository.

Its note guesses the runner's output capture is at fault: 'the response DOES lead with a bold recommendation when captured by hand ... which points at the runner's output capture'. Captured through --json on 2026-08-23, the graded string begins:

    Add a nullable column.\n\n| Option | Work to build | ...

The response leads with the recommendation, on the first line, above the table. The rule is satisfied. The grader is `\\A\\s*(\\*\\*|#{2,} )`, which requires markdown bold or a heading, so it fails a response that follows the rule in plain prose.

This is the second time this case has been failed by a formatting proxy. Its own `why` records the first: an earlier pattern demanded the literal word 'recommend' and failed 3 of 3 correct responses.

The stakeholder is anyone shipping through /tadw:ship, and the author of any future style rule graded by proxy.
design:
Grade the rule the case exists to measure: the recommendation LEADS. Deterministically, that is 'the first line names one of the three options, before any table pipe'.

    \\A[^|\\n]{0,120}?(nullable column|side table|JSON)

Naming the options is specific to this case, which is correct: the case is specific, and a general 'is this a recommendation' pattern is the proxy that failed twice already.

What it accepts and rejects is the test of whether the bar moved to the right place, so pin both directions with fixtures rather than only re-running the model.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Given the real response captured on 2026-08-23, when the grader runs, then it passes.
2. Given a response that opens with the table and states the recommendation after it, when the grader runs, then it fails.
3. Given a response that opens with a preamble naming no option, when the grader runs, then it fails.
4. Given the case file, when it is read, then known_failing is gone and the why records what the two proxies got wrong.
5. Given the repository, when python3 evals/run.py runs, then decision-matrix-trigger passes in both arms.
close_reason: shipped: fix: grade decision-matrix-trigger on the rule, not the markup (tadw-z3q)

title: Pin the typed /quality-gates path with a UserPromptSubmit regression case
description:
## Why (Computational)

.claude/settings.json wires UserPromptSubmit to label_bead_on_skill_invocation.sh so a typed
/quality-gates drops the gate marker. That command reads SKILL.md rather than invoking the
skill, so PreToolUse never fires for it and UserPromptSubmit is the only event that sees it.

hooks/test-claude-scripts.sh covers the Skill-tool path (label/pre, :586) and a typed
/tadw:build (label/prompt, :676), but no case fires UserPromptSubmit with /quality-gates. The
most-used entry point is verified by hand only. Verified working manually on 2026-08-22 against
a throwaway repo; nothing stops it from breaking silently.

## Estimated size

1 file, ~15 LOC, band: Trivial.
design:
Add one case to hooks/test-claude-scripts.sh beside the existing label/prompt case, using
the same payload helper with event UserPromptSubmit and command /quality-gates. Assert the
marker file exists and that its third line names the skill, matching what the label/pre case
asserts for the Skill-tool path.

Note for whoever writes it: the Stop path requires the report to be strictly newer than the
marker in whole seconds, so a case that writes the report in the same second reads as "the run
is still going". The existing PASS case handles this; a new one must too.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Given hooks/test-claude-scripts.sh, when it runs, then a case fires UserPromptSubmit with the command /quality-gates and asserts the gate marker is dropped naming the skill.
2. Given that case, when the UserPromptSubmit wiring is removed from .claude/settings.json or the prompt mapping is reverted in the hook, then the case fails.

title: Strip redirecting credentials before each eval model call
description:
## Why (Computational)

`evals/run.py` spawns `claude -p` with the parent environment inherited whole. When the shell exports `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, that key takes precedence over the stored claude.ai login and every case fails at invocation with a connectors warning that reads like a style failure. Measured 2026-08-22: 12 of 12 runs failed that way, and the harness reported 0/6 in both arms.

The same class of variable can redirect the call without failing it. `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK` with `AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK` routes to a different account, and `ANTHROPIC_MODEL` can answer with a model other than the one the run header reports.

The stakeholder is anyone who runs the declared check list from a shell that was switched to another account. `evals/run.py` is in the AGENTS.md command list, so a ship gate hits this and reports a blocked repository that is fine.

`evals/README.md` already names the fix: run `env -u ANTHROPIC_API_KEY python3 evals/run.py` "until run.py strips that variable itself".
design:
Build the child environment in one place, at the single spawn point in `ask()`, from an explicit named tuple of the variables that redirect a call. Do not filter by prefix: `ANTHROPIC_` would also drop unrelated settings, and a named list says why each entry is there.

Strip rather than warn. A warning inside a 12-call run scrolls past, and the failure it warns about is total.

Shorten the `evals/README.md` passage to state the behavior instead of the workaround.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Given a shell exporting ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, when a case runs, then the spawned claude process does not see that variable.
2. Given a shell exporting CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK and AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK, when a case runs, then the spawned process sees neither.
3. Given any run, when a case runs, then the spawned process still sees the rest of the parent environment, PATH included.
4. Given the repository, when python3 evals/test_run.py runs, then it passes and covers the rule above without a model call.
5. Given evals/README.md, when it describes running the suite, then it no longer tells the reader to strip the variable by hand.
close_reason: shipped: fix: strip redirecting credentials before eval model calls (tadw-6x4)

title: Add the domain-modeling skill
description:
## Why (Computational)

tadw has no shared-language discipline. Every session re-derives a project's jargon from the code,
so agents spend tokens explaining concepts the author already has one word for, and names drift
across sessions.

Adapted from Matt Pocock's `domain-modeling` skill (MIT, https://github.com/mattpocock/skills),
reviewed at ~/local/src/mattpocock-skills.

## How (Algorithmic)

1. New `skills/domain-modeling/SKILL.md`: the active discipline (challenge a term against the
   glossary, sharpen fuzzy terms, stress-test with scenarios, cross-check against code, update
   `CONTEXT.md` inline).
2. New `skills/domain-modeling/CONTEXT-FORMAT.md`: the glossary format, single- and multi-context.
3. Do NOT copy their ADR-FORMAT.md. tadw already owns ADRs in `architecture-decision-record`,
   which writes to `docs/decisions/`, not `docs/adr/`. Keep their three-part offer gate and
   delegate the format.
4. Register: the AGENTS.md name list, the routing table, and the README skills table.

## Estimated size

2 new files, 2 edited, about 90 lines, band: Small.
acceptance_criteria:
- `skills/domain-modeling/SKILL.md` and `skills/domain-modeling/CONTEXT-FORMAT.md` exist and `claude plugin validate .` passes
- The skill delegates ADR creation to the `architecture-decision-record` skill and never names `docs/adr/`
- `domain-modeling` appears in the AGENTS.md skill list with the count updated, plus the routing table and the README skills table
- `rumdl fmt --check .` and `python3 skills/quality-gates/scripts/check_doc_paths.py` pass

title: Add the grilling skill and the /grill-me command
description:

title: Revise the quality-gates fan-out plan to match ADR 0002
description: ADR 0002 amends docs/plans/quality-gates-agent-refactor.md in three ways but tadw-lm2 does not authorize editing the plan, so the plan and its child beads still carry the pre-ADR design. The agent filename becomes agents/quality-gates-orchestrator.md, the fan-out drops from four lanes to three (Gate 5 folds into the orchestrator), and criterion 7's labeling mechanism moves from an injected instruction to gate mode against quality-gates-report.json. title: Restructure the quality-gates skill's Step 4 into lanes
description:
## Why (Computational)

Step 4 spans `skills/quality-gates/SKILL.md:196-467` as one sequential block. The orchestrator
cannot partition what the skill states as a single pass, and three cross-gate couplings currently
survive by convention rather than by statement, so a future edit breaks them silently:

- Gate 7 takes its `--base` from the SHA Step 2 resolved (`SKILL.md:102`).
- Gate 2 cites Gate 8's result, and a green Gate 8 does not satisfy Gate 2's end-to-end rule
  (`SKILL.md:217`, `:243`).
- A browser-ui surface is a HANDOFF this skill cannot settle (`SKILL.md:220`,
  `route_qa.py:85`), and it rides its own row.

## Estimated size

1 file, 180 LOC, band: Target.
design:
Partition Step 4 by the lane table in `docs/plans/quality-gates-agent-refactor.md`, and state each
of the three couplings inline where the gate that depends on it is defined, rather than leaving them
to be rediscovered.

The constraint that shapes the edit: the skill must remain a valid standalone document.
`skills/verify-acceptance/SKILL.md:89` reads it and runs four of its gates with no agent involved,
and the plan's rollback path depends on that staying true, since reverting the feature is deleting
the agent and restoring one line of the command.

Gate semantics do not change. Only the statement of who runs each gate, and in what grouping, does.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Given a change with an `http-api` surface, when the report is produced, then Gate 2's end-to-end finding and Gate 8's probe result are both present and distinguishable, per `SKILL.md:243`.
2. Given a fixture diff containing a `.tsx` file, when the gates run, then a `Handoff: browser-ui` row naming `/qa` appears with a null command, Gate 2 is reported HANDOFF rather than SKIP because every routed surface was a handoff, and the verdict is INCOMPLETE.
3. Given a diff touching both an `http-api` file and a `library` file, when the gates run, then the report carries exactly one Change coverage row whose counts cover every case in the numbered case list, and the Change Coverage table carries a row for every numbered case.
4. Given the restructured skill, when `/verify-acceptance` reads it, then it runs its four gates without the agent.
notes:
## Done when (Acceptance)

• Every gate resolves to exactly one lane or to the orchestrator
• All three couplings are stated in the skill rather than implied
• /verify-acceptance can still read the skill directly and run its four gates with no agent

## Out of scope

• Changing what any gate checks. This is a restatement of ownership, not of technique.

## Implementation (2026-08-22, commit a814d94)

Step 4 of skills/quality-gates/SKILL.md gained three subsections at its head:

- **Who Runs Each Gate**: states the standalone shape first (verify-acceptance reads this file and runs four gates with no agent), then the three-lane partition. An 11-row ownership table covers every row the report can contain, including the two rows Step 4 never defined before (handoff rows, Project checks). Also states the blocking-dispatch rule from ADR 0002 Finding 4, the undispatched-lane SKIP rule, and the missing-return BLOCKED rule.
- **What Every Lane Is Given, and What It Must Not Re-derive**: base SHA, changed paths, gate set, numbered case list.
- **Reducing Two Rows for One Gate**: per-field reduction (status, counts, evidence tables, raw output, attribution), with the handoff row exempt.

Couplings stated inline at the depending gate: base SHA at Gate 7, the Gate 8 citation at Gate 2, browser-ui HANDOFF in the new Handoff Rows subsection.

Follows ADR 0002: three lanes, not four. Gate 5 and the docs-surface Gate 2 row moved to the orchestrator.

Also added: ownership sentences in Step 5 and Step 6, two Always rules, two Never rules, two checklist items.

Gate semantics unchanged. +144/-2 lines, one file.

title: Keep bead labeling working when the gates run from an agent
description:
## Why (Computational)

`.claude/settings.json:29` wires `.claude/scripts/label_bead_on_skill_invocation.sh` to
`PreToolUse` with matcher `Skill`, and that copy maps `quality-gates` to inject mode at `:202-204`,
carrying the gate "the overall verdict is PASS". An agent dispatch is not a `Skill` call, so the
hook never fires and never errors: the label silently stops being applied.

The plan's risk table rates this the most likely failure of the whole change, because nothing
reports it.

Two tracked copies of the hook exist and they have diverged. The `.claude/scripts/` copy handles
`PreToolUse` and `Stop` only; the `scripts/` copy ships to other repositories, is wired to three
events, and uses gate mode instead of inject mode.

## Estimated size

4 files, 90 LOC, band: Target.
design:
Implement whichever mechanism the ADR chose: an added matcher for the agent dispatch, having the
orchestrator invoke the skill through the Skill tool so the existing matcher still fires, or
labeling from the Stop event.

Touch both copies deliberately rather than editing one and assuming they match. The `.claude/`
copy is what fires in this repository; the `scripts/` copy is what the installer distributes.

Extend `hooks/test-claude-scripts.sh` with a case that fails when the labeling path breaks. The
suite already fakes the tracker on PATH and asserts recorded argv, so the case fits the existing
harness. Without it this defect can only be found by noticing an absent label.

1. Given a /quality-gates run started by a typed command or by the Skill tool, when it starts, then the hook drops a gate-mode marker naming the bead and the skill, and injects no instruction.
2. Given <git-dir>/quality-gates-report.json written after that marker with verdict PASS, when the session stops, then the bead carries the qa-d label; given FAIL, INCOMPLETE, NO GATES RAN, or an unreadable file, then it carries no label and the marker is cleared; given a report older than the marker, then the marker is kept.

title: Add the quality-gates orchestrator agent with its four lane contracts
description:
## Why (Computational)

This is the component the plan exists to add. Without it the four lanes have no dispatcher, the
eight-field lane contract has no producer, and the aggregation rule has nowhere to live.

`/quality-gates` runs at every session close (`AGENTS.md:314`) and is a stated precondition for
`/tadw:ship` (`skills/ship/SKILL.md:20`), so this is the most frequently executed path in the
repository.

## Estimated size

1 file, 220 LOC, band: Target.
design:
One `agents/quality-gates.md` carrying the repo's four frontmatter fields (`name`,
`description`, `model`, `tools`), following the body shape `agents/code-reviewer.md` uses.

It owns Steps 1, 2, 3, and 6 of the skill, so no lane re-derives the gate set, the scope, or the
routing. It runs `changed_set.py` exactly once and passes the base SHA, the changed paths, the
discovered gate set, and the single numbered case list into every lane.

It runs Gates 3, 4, 6, and 7 itself, because each is one scripted command and dispatching a subagent
to run one `python3` call costs more than it saves. It also owns three rows no lane can produce: the
`Handoff: mobile-ui` row, the Project checks row (`SKILL.md:90`), and Gate 2's own HANDOFF status
when every routed surface is a handoff (`SKILL.md:180-181`), which no single lane can see.

Aggregation reduces duplicate graded rows per field, not on status alone: status by the stated
order, counts as a sum over the union of the case list, and every `evidence_block` spliced in
case-number order regardless of which status survived. A lane that fails to return is BLOCKED,
never PASS.

Take the lane table, the contract, and the reduction rule from
`docs/plans/quality-gates-agent-refactor.md` rather than re-deriving them; five review passes went
into that partition.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Given a change with a REST surface, when the agent runs, then the report contains one row per gate for all eight gates, using only the six statuses at `SKILL.md:66-73`, plus a `Handoff: <surface>` row per handoff surface and a Project checks row when Step 1 discovered a command that maps to no gate.
2. Given the same change, when the agent dispatches, then the report's Scope line names exactly one base SHA and the transcript shows exactly one `changed_set.py` invocation.
3. Given a change with no frontend files, when the agent runs, then the frontend lane's rows are reported SKIP with a stated reason rather than omitted.
4. Given a lane whose dispatch is deliberately made to fail, when the agent aggregates, then that lane's gates are BLOCKED and the verdict is FAIL.
5. Given the same diff run three times each way, when all six runs complete, then every wall-clock time is recorded and the agent's median is no more than 10 percent slower than reading the skill directly.
6. Given a run through the agent, when it completes, then `raw_output` is non-null only on FAIL or BLOCKED rows whose gate ran a command, and the agent's transcript holds no test-runner output from a lane whose gates all passed.
notes:
## Done when (Acceptance)

- Dispatching against a REST-surface diff produces rows for all eight gates, each carrying every
  field of the lane contract
- The report is the one the skill already specifies, with the same six statuses and the same
  verdict rules
- No lane renders the report or decides the verdict

## Out of scope

- Restructuring the skill's Step 4. That is a sibling bead, and this one reads the skill as it is.
- Repointing `commands/quality-gates.md` at the agent. That is the referrer bead.

title: Prove a plugin agent can dispatch a subagent, then record the four decisions
description:
## Why (Computational)

The quality-gates fan-out rests on a capability no component in this plugin has ever used. None of
the twelve files in `agents/` carries a Task or Agent tool, so milestones 2 through 4 of
`docs/plans/quality-gates-agent-refactor.md` are speculative until this returns an answer.

Three further decisions block the same work:

- Whether `commands/quality-gates.md` and `agents/quality-gates.md` collide in the `tadw:`
  namespace. `AGENTS.md:262-266` rules only on command-versus-skill.
- How bead labeling survives an agent dispatch. `.claude/settings.json:29` wires the hook to
  `PreToolUse` with matcher `Skill`, which an agent dispatch is not.
- Whether the documentation lane reports drift or fixes it. `commands/quality-gates.md:39` and
  `skills/quality-gates/SKILL.md:695` both promise report-only, so fixing reverses a guarantee.

## Estimated size

2 files, 180 LOC, band: Target.
design:
Spike first, decide second.

The spike is one throwaway agent that dispatches a trivial subagent and returns its result, deleted
once it has answered. It is not a prototype of the orchestrator; it answers one question, can the
dispatch happen at all.

Then one ADR under `docs/decisions/`, recording all four answers. Two of them have two known
candidates each rather than open research: the namespace question resolves either by having the
command read the agent by path (the dodge it already uses for the skill) or by naming the agent
`quality-gates-orchestrator`; the labeling question resolves by an added matcher, by having the
orchestrator invoke the skill through the Skill tool so the existing matcher fires, or by labeling
from the Stop event.

The ADR must also record the consequence the plan pre-commits to: if the documentation question
resolves to report-only, Gate 5 folds into the orchestrator and the fan-out becomes three lanes,
because Gate 5 is one scripted command (`SKILL.md:295-300`) and fails the same test that keeps Gates
3, 4, 6, and 7 in-process.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Given the spike, when it runs, then it either returns a subagent's result or reports the exact failure, and the ADR records which.
2. Given the dispatch proves impossible, when the ADR is written, then it selects the sequential fallback and states that plan criterion 9 degrades to a no-regression check.
3. Given the ADR, when read by someone who has not seen this bead, then each of the four questions carries a decision and a rationale.
4. Given the repository after the ADR lands, when `/validate-plugin` runs, then it passes.
notes:
## Done when (Acceptance)

- The spike has demonstrated a plugin agent dispatching a subagent and returning its result, or has
  proven it cannot, and the ADR records which
- The ADR states a decision and a rationale for each of the four questions
- No question is left open for a later milestone to rediscover
- `/validate-plugin` passes

## Out of scope

- Building the orchestrator. That is the next bead, and it starts from this bead's answers.

title: Automate tracker sync in the repo's own pre-push hook
description: Standing instruction from the repository owner, recorded under 'The author never handles tracker plumbing' in AGENTS.md: they will never run the tracker export by hand, and they will never remember to sync the Dolt remote. Today both are manual steps a session has to remember, so bead state reaches GitHub only when someone thinks of it. The beads git hooks that used to cover part of this were switched off deliberately, because core.hooksPath now points at .githooks so the repo's own 14 CI checks run again.
design:
Put the automation in .githooks/pre-push, not back in .beads/hooks. Reasons: it is tracked in git so the author can read it, it is already the gate that runs on every push, and it keeps one hook system instead of two. The two-copy split between .githooks and .beads/hooks is exactly what caused the 12-of-14 check drift.

Shape: after the checks pass and before the push proceeds, export the tracker and stage the export if it changed. Keep it silent on success and loud on failure, per rule 3 of the AGENTS.md block.

Open design questions for the author:
  - A pre-push hook cannot add a commit to the range being pushed. Staging an export mid-push either needs an amend (rewrites the commit being pushed) or a follow-up commit (leaves the push one commit behind). Neither is obviously right. The alternative is a Claude Code Stop hook, which runs while a session is still live and can commit normally.
  - Whether to also run the Dolt remote sync, or only the text export.

BLOCKED ON A BROKEN REMOTE. The Dolt sync path is not usable as it stands:
  - bd dolt remote list prints 'origin' with the GitHub URL.
  - bd dolt show prints 'Remotes: (none)'.
  - git ls-remote origin 'refs/dolt/*' returns nothing, so no bead data has ever synced that way.
Those two commands disagree, so the remote has to be settled before any automation can rely on it. Until then, automate the text export only, and leave the Dolt sync out.

Follow the existing hook conventions: report every failure rather than stopping at the first, warn by name when a tool is missing and allow the push, and honor TADW_PREPUSH=off. Add cases to .githooks/test_prepush.py, which already drives real git push --dry-run runs in a throwaway fixture.
acceptance_criteria:
1. A push carries current tracker state without anyone running an export command.
2. On success the hook prints nothing about the tracker.
3. On failure the hook says what failed and that beads now exist on one machine only.
4. A missing bd binary warns by name and allows the push, matching the existing convention.
5. TADW_PREPUSH=off still skips everything, including the new step.
6. .githooks/test_prepush.py covers the success path, the failure path, and the missing-bd path, and the whole suite passes.
7. The Dolt remote disagreement above is either resolved and the sync automated, or recorded as out of scope with the text export automated alone.
8. No workflow document asks a person to run an export.

title: /build (feature-development): accept a bead id or a Linear URL
description: /tadw:build is used in both work and personal repositories, but Phase 1 grounds the spec from bd fields only. Work issues live in Linear, so the skill cannot read the spec it is asked to build in a work repository. Unlike verify-acceptance, /build also accepts a free-form feature description, so the argument parse has a third form to keep separate.
design:
commands/build.md already interpolates $ARGUMENTS, so only its argument-hint widens to [bead-id | linear-url | feature-description].

Parse order matters here. Treat the argument as an id ONLY when the entire argument, anchored, is a linear.app URL, a bare [A-Z][A-Z0-9]+-[0-9]+, or a lowercase bead id. Anything else is a feature description, otherwise 'add OAUTH2-2 fallback' is read as Linear issue OAUTH2-2.

skills/feature-development/SKILL.md Phase 1 (lines 32-68) gains a third mode beside the bead-id and no-bead-id modes. The buildability gate (lines 44-50) reads four separate bd fields and a Linear issue has one description body, so two of its five rows lose their input:
  - acceptance_criteria comes from a criteria or Done-when section in the description, the same rule as tadw-c99.
  - design (the How) also comes from that body, so criteria and approach stop being separable.
  - the notes too-big row has no Linear equivalent and degrades to 'not stated'. Say that out loud rather than inventing a size judgment.
  - exists/closed, status, and assignee map to the Linear state and assignee from get_issue.

Keep ONE gate table keyed on the questions rather than the bd field names, plus a short note on where each answer lives in Linear. A second table drifts from the first.

Also: line 47 sends vague criteria to bead-audit, which cannot audit a Linear issue, so the Linear path reports the gap inline and stops. Lines 28 and 29 point at /plan-to-beads and bead-audit, both bead-only, and need the same tracker-aware test as tadw-c99 (bd on PATH and .beads/ exists). Line 52 forbids claiming and closing in bd terms and must name the Linear writes too, since that MCP exposes save_issue. Line 61 output Source allows 'Linear ENG-45'. (The stale tracker name in the description on line 3 was already fixed on 2026-08-21.)

Phases 2 through 5 are tracker-agnostic and need no change; 'bead' there is only the word for the spec.

Deliberately NOT extracting the shared resolution rule into a reference file. Two callers is duplication, not a pattern; extract on the third, per the house core.
acceptance_criteria:
1. /build <bead-id> behaves exactly as today.
2. /build <linear-url> and /build <TEAM-123> read the issue, ground the spec from its description, and restate the criteria as the build checklist.
3. /build 'add OAUTH2-2 fallback' is treated as a feature description, not as Linear issue OAUTH2-2.
4. The buildability gate runs on the Linear path, keying on the questions, and reports the too-big row as 'not stated' rather than judging size.
5. Vague Linear criteria stop the run with the gap reported inline, citing no bead-audit.
6. The Do-NOT-use list no longer points a work repository at /plan-to-beads or bead-audit.
7. The skill issues no Linear write of any kind, and still does not claim, re-status, or close anything.
8. claude plugin validate . passes, and check_doc_paths.py passes.

title: verify-acceptance: accept a bead id or a Linear URL
description: /verify-acceptance today grades only beads. Work projects track issues in Linear, personal projects in bd, so the skill is unusable in half of the repositories it is invoked from. The command also declares argument-hint but never interpolates $ARGUMENTS, so a named target cannot reach the skill at all.
design:
Command layer (commands/verify-acceptance.md): widen argument-hint to [bead-id | linear-url], add a labeled '**Target:** $ARGUMENTS' line so an empty expansion stays readable, widen the description and the step-1 summary on line 14 and the note on line 22.

Skill layer (skills/verify-acceptance/SKILL.md): rewrite Step 1 (lines 34-56) as a dispatch on argument shape. The whole argument must match, anchored: a linear.app URL or a bare [A-Z][A-Z0-9]+-[0-9]+ goes to Linear via mcp__plugin_linear_linear__get_issue; a lowercase bead id goes to bd show <id> --json. Extract the identifier after /issue/ and discard the slug, fragment, and query string.

No argument means tracker-aware auto-resolution, using the test ship already uses (bd on PATH and .beads/ exists, skills/ship/SKILL.md:136). Tracker present keeps todays bd-first chain. Tracker absent skips bd, looks for a Linear identifier in the branch name, then commit messages, then asks.

Criteria for a Linear issue come from the description body only: a '## Acceptance Criteria' or '## Done when' heading, then top-level '- [ ]' checkboxes, then NONE RECORDED. Not comments, not sub-issues, so the result stays deterministic. On the Linear path drop the bead-audit pointer in Step 2, since bead-audit cannot audit a Linear issue.

Also: widen the skill description (line 3), the Unit-of-work and Resolved-by lines in the output template, the wording on lines 24 and 149, and add a Never rule forbidding every Linear write (save_issue, save_comment, status change). (The stale tracker name on line 112 was already fixed on 2026-08-21.)

Fail closed on both paths: a named issue that does not exist, or an unavailable Linear tool, reports what is missing and stops. No fallback to auto-resolution and no grading from the diff.

Out of scope: the labeling hook needs no guard, because Linear is only used in work repositories where that hook is not installed. tadw:ship stays bead-only and already routes PR repositories to /pr-maintain.
acceptance_criteria:
1. /verify-acceptance <bead-id> grades that bead, unchanged from today.
2. /verify-acceptance <linear-url> resolves the issue, reads criteria from its description, and grades them.
3. /verify-acceptance <TEAM-123> resolves the same way as the URL form.
4. /verify-acceptance with no argument in a repo with .beads/ uses todays bd-first chain.
5. /verify-acceptance with no argument in a repo without .beads/ tries the branch name for a Linear identifier, then asks. It never reports UNRESOLVED solely because bd is absent.
6. A Linear issue with no criteria section reports 'Criteria: NONE RECORDED' and an INCONCLUSIVE acceptance half, and cites no bead-audit.
7. An unreachable Linear tool reports what is missing and stops, with no fallback to auto-resolution.
8. The skill issues no Linear write of any kind.
9. claude plugin validate . passes, and check_doc_paths.py passes.

title: AGENTS.md said the tracker never auto-commits, but a hook committed and pushed bead state
description:
`AGENTS.md` under "Issue Tracking" stated that the tracker never auto-commits or runs git
commands, and that all git operations are explicit. That was not true of this clone.

Observed on 2026-08-11: a single tracker claim on tadw-qg-json-verdict-artifact-21l produced
commit b65ba55 "beads: state update", and that commit reached origin/main with no explicit git
command in the session. `.claude/scripts/autocommit_beads_after_br.sh` is what did it, ported in
commit 9ce0f8a.

Why it mattered: a session that reads AGENTS.md believes its tracker calls are inert, so it claims
a bead while exploring, or during a rebase, and finds an unexpected commit on main. The stated
invariant is the one a session plans around.

Resolved 2026-08-21 by deleting the hook rather than by documenting it. It existed only because the
old tracker wrote its state into a git-tracked export; `bd` writes to a gitignored database and
refreshes the export in place, so nothing auto-commits and the AGENTS.md statement is true again.
close_reason: Obsolete: .claude/scripts/autocommit_beads_after_br.sh was deleted on 2026-08-21 in the bd-only cutover, so no hook commits or pushes tracker state any more. AGENTS.md now reads 'Issue Tracking (bd + bv)' and its 'never auto-commits' statement is true again.

title: Script the quality-gates JSON artifact write
description:
The artifact write landed as prose in `skills/quality-gates/SKILL.md` Step 5 (bead tadw-qg-json-verdict-artifact-21l). The model reassembles the schema on every run, and the pre-push consumer treats an unparseable or field-shifted artifact the same as no artifact: it warns and allows. So a drifted write disables the verdict gate without ever saying so, which is the exact silent-degradation failure mode the doc-freshness and secrets gates were scripted to avoid.

Design: a stdlib-only `skills/quality-gates/scripts/write_report_json.py` mirroring `check_doc_paths.py` and `check_secrets.py` conventions. It takes the gate rows and the verdict on stdin as JSON, derives head, dirty, and timestamp from git itself rather than trusting the caller to retype them, validates `verdict` against the four Verdict Rules strings, and exits 2 when the tree is not a git repository. Then point Step 5 at the script instead of at the inline python3.

Not folded into tadw-qg-json-verdict-artifact-21l on purpose: that bead's own estimate is 3 files and 80 LOC of prose, and a script plus its pinned suite is a separate unit of roughly 300 LOC.

title: Teach the eval harness to run in a fixture repository
description:
## Why (Computational)

`evals/run.py` hardcodes `cwd=REPO_ROOT` inside `ask()`, so every case runs against
this repository and no case can plant a defect. That single line is why the skill's behavior has
never been tested.

The stakeholder is any future editor of `skills/quality-gates/SKILL.md`, who today has no
regression signal at all: every rule not converted into a script is unprotected prose.

Plan: docs/plans/quality-gates-hardening.md (M6)

## Estimated size

2 files, about 160 LOC, band: Target.
design:
Two optional `case.json` keys, both backward compatible with the six existing
cases.

A `fixture` key names a directory under `evals/fixtures/`. The harness copies it to a temp
directory, initializes it as a git repository with one commit, applies the case's planted defect,
and passes that directory as `cwd` instead of `REPO_ROOT`.

A `single_arm` key runs only the with-plugin arm. A slash command does not exist without the
plugin, so a baseline arm would measure nothing and would double the cost of every run. This is
recorded as D7 in the plan.

Keep the existing regex graders. These assertions are about which verdict and status words appear
in the report, which `require_regex` and `forbid_regex` already handle well. No judge is needed,
and adding one would make the suite nondeterministic for no gain.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Given the six existing cases, when `python3 evals/run.py` runs, then all six behave exactly as before the change.
2. Given a case with a `fixture` key, when it runs, then the model's working directory is a temp copy of that fixture with its own git history, not the repository root.
3. Given a case with `single_arm` set to true, when it runs, then only the with-plugin arm executes.
4. Given `evals/README.md`, when reading it, then both keys are documented with the reason fixture cases skip the baseline arm.
notes:
## Done when (Acceptance)

- `run.py` honors `fixture` and `single_arm`, both optional
- The six existing response-style cases pass unchanged
- A fixture case runs against a temp git repository, not the repository root
- `evals/README.md` documents both keys and why fixture cases are single-arm

## Out of scope

The fixture cases themselves. Those are the two eval-case beads that depend on this one.
